findings.issue_text: Blacklist comparison lowercases entries but not submitted guest addresses, allowing mixed-case emails to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
Team authorization uses isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner instead of ||, denying legitimate admins and owners because the roles are mutually exclusive
sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, so resubmitted existing attendees are treated as new and receive scheduled-booking emails
Guest deduplication only checks existing attendees and not duplicates within the submitted list, allowing direct API calls to insert duplicate attendee rows
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings and queues organizer and attendee notifications for events configured to suppress them

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same security vulnerability as the golden comment: the blacklist check lowercases the blacklist entries but not the submitted guest email addresses, allowing attackers to bypass the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction by using mixed-case/uppercase characters in their email submissions.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: Team authorization uses isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner instead of ||, denying legitimate admins and owners because the roles are mutually exclusive
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same problem as the golden comment: the code incorrectly uses AND (&&) instead of OR (||) when checking team admin/owner permissions. Both comments point out that this logic is wrong because the roles are mutually exclusive (or at minimum, a user only needs to be one or the other), so using && would incorrectly deny access to legitimate admins and owners.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, so resubmitted existing attendees are treated as new and receive scheduled-booking emails
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies a problem with sendAddGuestsEmails receiving raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, which causes existing attendees to be treated as new and receive wrong emails. The golden comment describes the same underlying issue - the function passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array and checks against newGuests (the input guests array), which causes incorrect email type determination. Both are pointing to the same bug where the guest filtering/deduplication isn't properly applied before the email logic, resulting in wrong email types being sent.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the uniqueGuests/guest deduplication logic only checks against existing attendees (and blacklisted emails) but does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted input list itself, which could allow duplicate attendee rows to be inserted via createMany. Both comments point to the same bug regarding missing internal deduplication of the input.

Both comments point to the same bug - missing validation of the disableStandardEmails flags before sending notifications.
